messages:
Ana: APAC inference cluster showing a large GPU pending backlog — ~60 pods Pending for ~12m, autoscaler not reacting.
Mike: Which nodepool?
Ana: apac-gpu-pool-1. `kubectl get pods -n inference` shows many with "0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" even though nodes report Ready.
ops-bot: [Alert] apac-gpu-pool-1 approaching ENI/vCPU quota, cluster-autoscaler event: scale up suppressed (backoff_rate_limited).
Julie: Cloud provider logs show ENI quota errors and repeated 429s on instance create.
Sam: CA logs: "Scale up failed: node creation failed: rate limited" then "Backoff for apac-gpu-pool-1" — looks like API throttling.
Leo: We also have a runaway controller: `ml-batch-train-2026` keeps spawning ~20 pods/min in inference-batch namespace. Controller loop or bad retry backoff.
Mike: Can we pause the orchestrator / controller?
Sam: Not from the cluster — it's managed by external ML orchestrator. Scaling the job to 0 just gets recreated.
Julie: Quick mitigation ideas: admission control to block the job, cordon nodes, taint to prevent scheduling, and spin up a small burst pool with preemptibles.
Ana: Implementing plan: cordon apac-gpu-pool-1 nodes, taint them `gpu-pressure=true:NoSchedule`, create `apac-gpu-burst` (preemptible) 6-node pool, and open cloud quota escalation for ENI/vCPU.
Mike: Cordon + taint applied to 4 problematic nodes.
ops-bot: [Action] apac-gpu-burst pool requested: 6 preemptible nodes provisioning.
Sam: Cloud API still returning 429s but some preemptibles are provisioning in a different AZ — partial success.
Leo: Deployed fast Admission webhook to throttle pod creation from `inference-batch` namespace (temporary soft limit 5/min).
Julie: Also added temporary PodDisruptionBudget exceptions and evicted low-priority batch pods to free GPUs for critical inference pods.
Mike: After cordon + taint + webhook, pending GPU pods dropped from ~60 -> 8 in ~10m. Cluster Autoscaler successfully provisioned 6 nodes in `apac-gpu-burst` and scheduler bound highest-priority pods.
Sam: Cloud quota team filed an expedited ENI/vCPU request. We should expect more stable provisioning after quota uplift.
Ana: Immediate mitigations worked. Follow-ups: 1) add rate-limits and backoff on ML orchestrator; 2) create a warm GPU pool (2-4 nodes) in APAC to reduce ENI spikes; 3) adjust CA backoff thresholds to treat ENI quota errors differently and consider cross-AZ provisioning; 4) add PodPriority classes for batch vs latency-sensitive workloads.
Leo: I'll own the runbook and include: cordon+taint commands, admission webhook snippet, warm-pool sizing recommendation, and a cloud quota escalation template.
Julie: Raising P1 for the follow-ups and assigning owners. I'll create the incident doc and link in #incidents.
Ana: Closing thread once postmortem + runbook PR merged. Thanks all :thumbsup:
